newsitem.title: UK: Pru extends grip on insurance market.
newsitem.headline: Pru extends grip on insurance market.

text.p: British insurance group Prudential Corp offered to increase its control in financial services group St James Place Capital on Wednesday, a move which would reinforce its position as the country's largest insurer.

Prudential, which recently bought Scottish Amicable for 2.87 billion pounds ($4.7 billion), said it had offered 130 pence a share for the 30.5 million shares representing 7.7 percent of St James, for a total 39.6 million pounds.

Through its ownership of Scottish Amicable, Prudential already held 25 percent in insurance firm J.Rothschild Assurance which is now being fully taken over by St James, the company announced on Wednesday.
St James already had 51 percent in J. Rothschild.
St James is offering 1.75 new shares for each J. Rothschild share held and will issue 43.3 million new shares to buy 32.1 million J. Rothschild convertible preference shares.
As such, Prudential will eventually control 118.8 million shares or 29.9 percent of St James Capital.

J. Rothschild has total funds of 1.7 billion pounds under its management. The group was one of Britain's fastest growing insurance firms in 1996 with a 39 percent growth rate, compared with 24 percent for the industry.
Prudential and Scottish Amicable have given an undertaking not to change the stake in the first year unless it is subject to an offer from a third party.

"That assurance from (Prudential chief executive) Peter Davis was fundamental to the deal," Mike Wilson, who will become chief executive of St James, told Reuters. Wilson is currently the chief executive of J. Rothschild.

A Prudential spokesman said the group believed it was in the long-term interests of St James and Prudential shareholders that St James should be independently managed and maintain a separate stock listing.
"This investment adds another string to Prudential's bow. It's a long-term investment for Prudential's shareholders," the spokeman said.

This is expected to increase Prudential's exposure to the upper end of the personal financial services market by bringing it closer to J. Rothschild's high-profile client base known to comprise a few very wealthy customers.
"Prudential believes that J. Rothschild Assurance has developed a high quality, focused distribution channel with a highly productive salesforce targeting high net worth individuals," it said.
In 1996 J. Rothschild contributed 11 million pounds towards St James's pretax profits of 33.2 million.
The news sent St James share price to a high of 134 pence, up from 125-1/2 on a trade volume of more than 10.75 million shares. Prudential's shares rose to 564p, up six pence.
The transactions would also bring Prudential closer to Life Assurance Holding Corporation in which St James holds 31.25 percent.

Life Assurance, created in 1994 in association with New York Life, has so far played an active role in the restructuring of Britain's life assurance industry by acquiring defunct life companies to run their continuing policies.
